Native background window, and turning debugging on only for short ADB sessions.
DroidHand only connects outward, to a relay on your own computer (ideally over Tailscale).
Must start with ws:// or wss://
Saved automatically. The agent reconnects when you leave this screen.
Where the agent works while you keep using the phone.
The agent uses its own window when it can turn debugging on (your keyboard is not affected); otherwise the native one.

Window drawn by the system. Works with debugging off. Note: while it is on screen, your keyboard closes whenever the agent touches it or opens a new screen in it, which makes typing hard. Tap the close button (square with an X) to close it.
Does not disturb your keyboard. Can be hidden, resized, made translucent and used. Turns debugging on only while the window is open, and closes if the phone screen turns off.
Not running · the agent starts it over ADB
Use Material You colors from your wallpaper.
Let the agent log ideas for new DroidHand features on your computer. Off by default.
The token field is always reported as a password to the agent, even when shown.
Every action is recorded in an append-only audit log on your computer.
The small red button on screen cancels the agent\'s current action; the agent is told and nothing needs re-enabling. To fully disconnect, use the notification or this app.
Ask before using the main screen
If you are using the phone, the agent asks before tapping or typing on your screen. Background windows never ask.
Acts on your screen without asking
Let the agent use your screen?
You are using the phone. The agent wants to tap and type on the main screen. The red button cancels it anytime.
Dangerous: full access to your phone

With this on, the agent can unlock your phone by itself and reach everything on it: banking, email, messages, passwords and verification codes. Anyone who controls the agent, your computer or the relay gets the same power. Use only if you understand and accept the risk.
Uses the saved PIN on the lock screen. One wrong attempt turns this off automatically.

Disclaimer: this feature is provided as is, without warranty of any kind. You alone decide to enable it and are solely responsible for any access, loss or damage that results. The DroidHand authors and contributors are not liable. The PIN stays encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore) and is never sent to the agent or the relay.
DroidHand closed the background window: its on-screen controls could not be shown.
Hide background window (the agent keeps working)
Not connected to the relay. Connect first to see its status.
This relay does not show its status (update DroidHand on the computer).
Only phones marked as admin on the relay can see its status.
Not seen since the relay started
Phones are listed from the computer\'s devices.json. Add one below; change or remove them on the computer.
No admin phone? Everything can be done on the computer instead:
Create a token for the new phone. Replace <id> with a short name (lowercase letters, digits, - or _), e.g. tablet.
Add the phone to ~/.config/droidhand/devices.json, inside \"devices\" (put a comma after the previous entry):
\"role\": \"admin\" lets the phone open this Relay screen. For a test phone whose ADB is always on, add \"adb\": { \"mode\": \"always\", \"serial\": \"<ip>:5555\" }.
Restart the relay so it reads the new phone:
Under Connection, enter the same relay address this phone uses: %1$s, and paste the new phone\'s token. The computer prints it with:

In the Permissions panel, turn on Accessibility (if it is greyed out: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings), Notifications and Unrestricted battery. On Samsung also: Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → DroidHand.
Once, from the computer: turn on Wireless debugging on the new phone, pair it (Pair device with pairing code, then adb pair <ip:port> on the computer), connect and run:
Then turn debugging off again: from now on the agent turns ADB on and off by itself when a task needs it.
With the new phone already connected over adb, this installs the app, sets the relay and token, turns accessibility on and does the one-time grant (run it in the droidhand folder):
The new phone shows up as connected in the Relay list. Agents pick a phone with device=\"<id>\" (list_devices shows them all).
Full guide: docs/setup.md, section \"Several phones\", in the project repository.
Give the new phone a name. The relay creates its token right away and this app builds an invite with the download link, the relay address and the token.
What agents pass as device=. Lowercase letters, digits, - and _.
Can open the Relay screen and add phones.
Connect this phone to the relay to add phones from the app.
Phone added. It can connect now.
The token is shown only now. Anyone with this invite can connect a phone to your relay: send it only to the new phone (or copy and paste it there).
No answer from the relay. Check the connection and try again.
The relay on the computer is older and cannot add phones. Update DroidHand on the computer, or use the steps below.
There is already a phone called %1$s.
Install Tailscale and sign in to the same tailnet as the computer.
Point the new phone\'s camera at the QR code to open the download page (or use this link), then install DroidHand:
In the new phone\'s DroidHand, open Connection → Scan QR code (or copy the invite there and tap Paste invite). The address and token are filled in.

DroidHand invite for %1$s

1. Get the app: %2$s
2. Open DroidHand → Connection → Paste invite (or fill in by hand):
Relay: %3$s
Token: %4$s
No invite on the clipboard. Copy the whole invite and try again.
This QR code is not a DroidHand invite.
Could not open the QR scanner (it needs Google Play services). Use Paste invite instead.
The QR code holds the download link, the relay address and the token. The new phone\'s camera opens the download page; DroidHand\'s Scan QR code connects.
